title: Pullback on cohomology over objects along a morphism of sites
statement: Let $f:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be a morphism of sites given by the continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with $f_*=u^s$, $f^{-1}$ its exact left adjoint on abelian sheaves and unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to f_*f^{-1}$. For $V\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $\mathcal A\in\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ choose an injective resolution $\mathcal A\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ and an injective resolution $f^{-1}\mathcal A\to\mathcal J^\bullet$; as $f^{-1}$ is exact, $f^{-1}\mathcal A\to f^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a resolution, so there is a map of complexes $\beta:f^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ under $f^{-1}\mathcal A$, unique up to homotopy. Define $f^*:H^p(V,\mathcal A)\to H^p(u(V),f^{-1}\mathcal A)$ as $H^p$ of $\Gamma(V,\mathcal I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\eta}\Gamma(V,f_*f^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet)=\Gamma(u(V),f^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\beta}\Gamma(u(V),\mathcal J^\bullet)$. Then: (1) $f^*$ does not depend on the choices, and in degree $0$ it is $\eta_{\mathcal A}(V):\mathcal A(V)\to(f^{-1}\mathcal A)(u(V))$; (2) $f^*$ is natural in $\mathcal A$: $H^p(f^{-1}\varphi)\circ f^*=f^*\circ H^p(\varphi)$ for $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$; (3) for a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A''\to0$ in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ the maps $f^*$ commute with the connecting maps of the long exact sequences of $H^\bullet(V,-)$ and of $H^\bullet(u(V),-)$ applied to the exact sequence $0\to f^{-1}\mathcal A\to f^{-1}\mathcal A'\to f^{-1}\mathcal A''\to0$; equivalently, $(f^*)_p$ is the unique morphism of $\delta$-functors $H^\bullet(V,-)\to H^\bullet(u(V),f^{-1}(-))$ extending $\eta(V)$ in degree $0$ ($H^\bullet(V,-)$ being universal); (4) for a second morphism of sites $g:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ given by $v:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$, so that $f\circ g$ is given by $v\circ u$, one has $(f\circ g)^*=H^p(c)\circ g^*\circ f^*$ on $H^p(V,\mathcal A)$, where $c:g^{-1}f^{-1}\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\sim}(f\circ g)^{-1}\mathcal A$ is the canonical isomorphism of left adjoints of $(f\circ g)_*=f_*g_*$ (compatible with the units).
